what: Charter Communications is the second-largest cable company in the United States. Under the Spectrum brand it sells broadband, television and mobile service to homes and businesses across 41 states.
customers: About 57 million passed homes and businesses, with roughly 30 million customer relationships.
money: Spectrum Mobile, which uses Verizon's network
moat: Cable plant passing tens of millions of homes, which cost decades and billions to build and which a competitor must overbuild street by street to challenge.
risks: Debt of about $107 billion is among the largest of any US company
Broadband subscribers have been falling as fixed wireless and fibre take share
It pays no dividend, using all free cash flow for buybacks and debt
opportunities: Spectrum Mobile is growing quickly and keeps broadband customers from leaving
Analysts see about 16% upside from current levels
Upgrading its network to higher speeds costs far less than building fibre from scratch
watch: Broadband subscriber net additions and mobile line growth.
